rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2-3, 3-year field experiment at Citra FL on Candler/Tavares sand with own yield, soil water, nitrate and root cores. Q2: Section 3.3, Tables 4-5, Fig. 5: root cores at three lateral positions show RLD concentrated under the drip/fertigation line, with 41% less RLD at 0.125 m and 70% less at 0.25 m from the line regardless of date; roots said to concentrate around the fertigation emitters. Q9: Section 3.3 reports RLD at P1 0-15 cm as 10.5 +/- 3.9 for SDI versus 2.6 +/- 1.7 and 2.5 +/- 0.9 cm cm-3 for SUR and TIME.
rows.notes: All three treatments are drip; there is no non-drip control, so the study shows the lateral root pattern under drip on sand but cannot isolate drip as cause. Lateral soil water movement was not measured (TDR and nitrate samples taken only near the drip line), so the intermediate variable is asserted, not measured. Root sampling only in 2006 and only at the 220 kg N rate; no yield harm from the root pattern is shown. No explicit limitations stated for the root result.

rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2-3, own 3-year field trial. Q2: Section 3.2 and Table 2: SMS-controlled SUR and SDI (five short daily windows, 10% VWC threshold) raised marketable yield 69-80% (2005), 20-26% (2006) and 11-21% (2007) over fixed-time irrigation, with higher above-ground biomass. Q4: Section 3.1 and Fig. 4: TDR at 0-25 and 25-55 cm shows SMS treatments kept soil moisture near constant with almost no percolation spikes, while TIME showed spikes draining within 12 h; Section 3.3 reports higher residual topsoil nitrate (32 and 12 vs 2 mg kg-1) under SMS treatments, linked to the yield benefit. Q8: Section 2: TIME used a twin line for experimental convenience whereas growers use one line; Section 3.1 and Conclusions: sensor position relative to the buried drip line inflated SDI water use; Section 3.2: 2005 results affected by disease and hot wet weather. Q9: Table 1 reports CV% for total and marketable yield and biomass in each year.
rows.notes: Single site, single soil, single crop (one cultivar), plot scale. Yield and biomass both from destructive harvest, so one method. Reduction in crop water stress is inferred from soil moisture, not measured in the plant.

rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2-3, own field trial. Q2: Section 3.1 and Fig. 4: SMS-based short irrigation events caused small soil moisture increases and decreased percolate volume, whereas TIME produced pronounced spikes at 0-25 and 25-55 cm indicating percolation through the profile; Section 3.3: residual nitrate at 74 DAT in 0-30 cm was 32 (SDI), 12 (SUR) and 2 (TIME) mg kg-1, authors state frequent small volumes kept the wetting front near the surface and reduced N displacement/leaching. Q3: two independent lines, TDR soil-water dynamics at two depths (Fig. 4) and KCl-extracted soil nitrate profiles (Section 3.3). Q4: soil water content and its exceedance of holding capacity measured by TDR is the mechanism linking small frequent applications to reduced leaching (Section 3.1, Fig. 4). Q8: Section 3.1: TDR position relative to the buried SDI line made moisture variations less distinct; rainfall contribution not considered though heavy events raised soil water; Section 2: TIME twin-line arrangement differs from commercial practice.
rows.notes: Leaching is inferred from soil moisture spikes and residual nitrate, not measured directly (no lysimeters or drainage flux). Nitrate profile reported for one date only, without dispersion. Single site, soil and crop.

rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2-3, own 3-year field trial with flowmeter-recorded irrigation. Q2: Section 3.1, Fig. 2, Conclusions: SMS-controlled SUR applied 15-51% less irrigation than fixed-time irrigation, SDI 7-29% less; iWUE ranked SUR > SDI > TIME (Table 2). Q4: Section 3.1 and Fig. 4: TDR soil moisture shows SMS treatments kept soil water near the threshold with events bypassed, while TIME irrigation exceeded holding capacity and drained. Q7: Section 3.1 and Conclusions: authors state from their data that water savings for SDI were low because the sensor averaged 0-20 cm while the drip line was buried at 15 cm, so sensor placement relative to the drip line governs the saving. Q8: Section 3.1 and Conclusions on probe positioning; Section 2 on TIME twin line not matching grower practice; rainfall not accounted for. Q9: Table 1 reports CV% for iWUE each year; savings given as a range across years.
rows.notes: Claimed 40-65% savings in the review exceed the study's 15-51% (SUR) and 7-29% (SDI). Water applied measured only by flowmeters (one method). Single site, soil, crop; plot scale.

rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2-3, own field trial. Q2: Section 3.2 and Table 2: SMS-based SUR and SDI increased marketable yield 69-80% (2005), 20-26% (2006), 11-21% (2007) versus TIME; biomass also higher. Q4: Fig. 4 and Section 3.3: soil moisture dynamics and residual topsoil nitrate measured and linked to the yield advantage. Q8: Section 2 TIME twin line for experimental convenience; Section 3.1 sensor placement issue for SDI; Section 3.2 disease and weather in 2005. Q9: Table 1 CV% for yield and biomass.
rows.notes: Review's 11-45% yield increase does not match the study's 11-80%. Single site, soil and crop; one harvest method.

rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2-3, own 3-year small-plot field trial. Q2: Section 2 and 3.1, Fig. 2, Conclusions: capacitance ECH2O probes with the QIC controller triggered irrigation at 10% VWC; SUR used 15-51% and SDI 7-29% less water than fixed-time drip irrigation on fresh-market tomato. Q4: Section 3.1, Fig. 4: TDR soil water shows bypassed events and absence of drainage spikes under sensor control. Q7: Section 3.1 and Conclusions: authors state sensor position relative to the buried drip line caused higher SDI water use, i.e. placement must match drip location. Q8: probe positioning limitation (Section 3.1, Conclusions); TIME twin-line arrangement unlike grower practice (Section 2). Q9: Table 1 CV% for iWUE; savings reported as ranges across years.
rows.notes: Flowmeter measurement only (single method). Single site, soil, crop; plot scale.

notes: Full text appears complete. Study is a 3-year plot experiment on one sandy site near Citra, Florida, one tomato cultivar; irrigation measured by flowmeters, soil water by TDR and ECH2O probes, nitrate by KCl extraction, roots by cores in 2006 only.
